subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should configured OpenAI-compatible memory embeddings inherit the provider’s three-state private-network contract: omitted means exact configured-origin trust, false denies private access, and true permits broader private-network access?
rationale: The code and proof establish a coherent implementation, but choosing implicit exact-origin compatibility versus explicit-only trust changes both existing-user upgrade behavior and the embedding SSRF boundary.

options.title: Approve three-state inheritance
options.body: Accept the documented omitted/false/true contract and land this patch as the canonical provider-policy integration.

options.title: Require explicit private opt-in
options.body: Revise omitted behavior to block private endpoints unless request.allowPrivateNetwork is explicitly true, accepting the resulting compatibility break or migration requirement.

options.title: Keep embeddings policy-isolated
options.body: Do not inherit provider request policy for embeddings and close or redesign the change around a separately approved memory trust contract.

recommendation.title: Approve three-state inheritance
recommendation.body: Accept the documented omitted/false/true contract and land this patch as the canonical provider-policy integration.

likelyOwner.reason: The exact-origin and explicit-denial semantics originate in Kaspre’s merged SSRF contract work, making that history the closest ownership signal for this decision.
